subject: Performance SLO qualification — latency & cost levers
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@novaretail.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + next steps (performance SLOs)

Hi Jordan — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned:

Summary of your goals
- Use-case: real-time chat for Nova Retail customer support (assist agents + shopper-facing chat widget)
- Traffic profile: peak concurrency ~350 users, sustained throughput target ~150 req/s during peak windows
- Payload: ~40–60 tokens per request on average (50 median)
- SLO targets: p95 latency target for token generation/streaming <= 250 ms (you mentioned 200–300ms range)
- Cost goal: reduce inference unit cost to fit within existing forecasts (target: <$2 / 1M tokens)

Immediate asks from Redwood
1) Confirm traffic profile (peak concurrency and peak sustained req/s) — we used values above from the call.
2) Clarify tolerable p95 window (is 250ms firm or would 300ms be acceptable for a material cost reduction?)
3) Any hard constraints on model family (open models acceptable?) and compliance needs (SOC 2 / data handling notes).

What we’ll deliver next (attached)
- A short SLO qualification doc with recommended cost/perf levers and expected latency estimates (redwood-performance-slo-proposal.pdf).
- Benchmark CSV with representative runs for the suggested model variants (slo-benchmark-results.csv).

High-level levers we think will get you to target
- Continuous batching (maintain small multi-request batches to amortize kernel overhead)
- Prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts (common for agent assist workflows)
- Quantized model variants (int8) — large latency reduction and cost savings with minimal quality regression for your use case
- Streaming response enabled (send incremental tokens to front-end to reduce perceived latency)
- Model fallbacks (13B quantized primary, 7B quantized fallback for bursts)

Next step: once you confirm the traffic tolerances above we’ll propose a config with expected p50/p95 and cost estimates, and schedule a technical deep-dive with Marcus and our infra team.

Thanks 
dMarissa
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0142

Attachment: redwood-performance-slo-proposal.pdf

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@novaretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps (performance SLOs)

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side:
- Peak concurrency: we see ~300–380 concurrent sessions during peak promo windows; 350 is a good planning number.
- Sustained peak throughput: closer to 140–160 req/s for the core chat feature; background async workloads are separate.
- Token distribution: median ~48, 90th ~95 tokens (rare), so planning on 50–60 average is safe.
- SLO flexibility: engineering prefers p95 <= 300ms if that materially reduces cost. If we can achieve <=250ms at acceptable cost, great — but 300ms acceptable.
- Model constraints: must be an open model or a model we can host in our VPC (no blackbox SaaS-only restrictions). SOC 2 is required — we’ll need your SOC 2 report and an overview of logging/audit capabilities.

Can you include a recommended production config (batching params, cache TTLs, quantization level, fallback rules) and an estimate of reserved capacity (GPUs / compute) for committed performance?

Also, can we do a 2-week canary on a subset (10% traffic) before a full roll?

—Jordan
Head of Engineering, Nova Retail
jordan.blake@novaretail.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@novaretail.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 11:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps (performance SLOs) — proposed config + estimates

Jordan — thanks, based on your clarifications we put together a recommended config and rough capacity/cost estimates (see attached PDF + CSV for raw benchmark runs). Key points below:

Recommended production config (starting point)\- Model: redwood-v1-13b-quant (int8) as primary; redwood-v1-7b-quant fallback for burst traffic\- Streaming: enabled (server-side incremental token flush) to minimize perceived latency for the frontend\- Continuous batching: target max_batch_size=64, max_latency_ms=20 (adaptive to traffic)\- Concurrency per worker: support up to 48 concurrent streams per GPU runtime (depends on instance type; benchmarked on A100-equivalent)\- KV/prefix caching: TTL 30m for common prompt prefixes (agent templates), cache hit expected 15–25% on first rollout\- Autoscaling: reserved pool of 4 GPU-equivalents with burstable capacity + on-demand for growth

Estimated perf (from bench runs, approximate)
- At 150 req/s, avg payload 50 tokens, streaming enabled, continuous batching: p50 token latency ~60–80 ms, p95 token latency ~180–220 ms (primary 13B int8)
- With fallback to 7B quantized for 20% of requests in bursts, effective p95 moves to ~240–300 ms during extreme bursts

Cost estimates
- Expected unit cost ~ $1.65 / 1M tokens with the recommended config and reserved capacity (subject to final reserved pricing)

Risk notes / tradeoffs
- Quantization (int8) reduces cost and latency but can produce minor quality differences on edge prompts. We recommend an eval set (we can run side-by-side) before final pinning.
- Continuous batching increases throughput efficiency but can add small tail latency; our adaptive max_latency_ms setting keeps p95 in target band.

Next steps
1) Marcus will run a targeted benchmark with a Nova prompt sample (can you share a redacted set of 20–30 representative prompts?).
2) Rishi / sales to draft reserved capacity numbers and a 2-week canary plan (10% traffic).
3) We’ll share SOC 2 and compliance docs via the secure drive link.

If this looks good I’ll schedule the infra deep-dive with Marcus and our ops team.

Thanks —
Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood-performance-slo-proposal.pdf, slo-benchmark-results.csv

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@novaretail.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps (performance SLOs) — reserved capacity + next steps

Jordan — quick note from the pricing/ops side. Appreciate the clarifications. Proposed commercial / rollout items:
- Reserved capacity recommendation: 4 x A100-equivalent GPU pool (dedicated) for initial production to hit sustained 150 req/s with headroom; add 2x as burst buffer if you want <200ms tail during promos.
- Canary: agree to a 2-week canary at 10% traffic. We’ll provide monitoring dashboards (latency, token counts, cache hit rate) and a rollback plan.
- Pricing: draft SOW + three pricing options (pay-as-you-go, 6-month commit, 12-month commit). 12-month commit will include a standard committed-discount; we can discuss tiered discounts for higher reserved capacity.
- Compliance: Marissa will send SOC 2 and audit docs to the secure drive.

Next steps
1) Jordan: share redacted prompt samples and confirm exact canary start date window.
2) Marcus: run the sample benchmarks and upload results to the linked drive.
3) Rishi/Marissa: send draft SOW and proposed reserved pricing by EOD next Tue (2027-04-20).

Jordan — happy to jump on a short call this week if you want to go over reserved pricing and options.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
